title: Jet Fuel Costs a Record High, So Holiday Flights Cost More
summary:
Do you hope to fly somewhere for the holidays? Your ticket will probably cost more this year.

The reason is jet fuel, the special fuel that planes burn. Fuel is one of the biggest costs for airlines, and its price just hit a record. On Thursday, jet fuel in the United States cost an average of $4.90 a gallon, said the tracking firm Argus. That is the highest price the firm has ever recorded, and more than twice last year's price.

Airlines are passing some of this cost to passengers. Hayley Berg, an economist at the travel company Hopper, said airfares are at a 10-year high. Thanksgiving tickets cost about 30% more than last year, and Christmas tickets are up more than 20%.

Still, most people are buying tickets. One Maryland traveler said family tickets cost too much, so she will drive to Chicago instead. Many others booked early to lock in a fare before prices climb higher.
why_it_matters: If your family flies to visit relatives for the holidays, higher ticket prices could change where you go or how you get there.
